name: Boris
label: Southern Lord
lede: A Tokyo trio that named itself after a Melvins song, played one hour-long drone, then spent thirty years refusing to sound like the last record.

eras.title: A name borrowed from the Melvins
eras.text: Boris formed in Tokyo in 1992 as a four-piece and took its name from a song on the Melvins' Bullhead. By 1996 the drummer was gone and Atsuo had moved behind the kit, making the trio that still exists.

years.h: Boris forms in Tokyo as a four-piece
years.p: Atsuo on vocals, [[Wata|0f61b915-11d8-4d09-b986-42280394c4ab]] on guitar, Takeshi on bass and Nagata on drums. The name comes from a track on the [[Melvins|9ccfbc94-a4f4-42f7-b6f5-d903ab77cccb]] album Bullhead.
years.xp: The band has said little about a grand plan; the Melvins and Earth-style slow, heavy drone were the starting template. According to Wikipedia, the name was taken from the Bullhead song of the same name.

years.h: Absolutego: one hour, one slow-motion track
years.p: Released on the band's own Fangs Anal Satan label, it runs about 60 minutes and the band always called it a single, not an album.
years.xp: It was the first release after original drummer Nagata left, with [[Atsuo|6adc77be-0df7-4818-ab6c-3faf11bbf709]] now drumming and Boris a three-piece. Its Melvins and Earth debt is obvious; Southern Lord later reissued it in 2001 as Absolutego+, remixed by Stephen O'Malley of [[Sunn O)))|1d3da898-4fb4-4445-b704-cd7315e01789]].

years.h: Nagata leaves and Atsuo takes the drum stool
years.p: The band continues as the trio of Atsuo, Wata and Takeshi, and none of them has changed since.

eras.title: Endless, then everything at once
eras.text: The first albums are long and low, then a single-take rock record and a 43-minute feedback piece set the pattern: no two Boris records alike. Southern Lord starts putting them out in America.

years.h: Amplifier Worship: first album, first Takeshi vocals
years.p: Five tracks and nearly 64 minutes on the Tokyo label Mangrove. It is where Takeshi first takes lead vocals on a Boris record.
years.xp: Southern Lord reissued it on CD in 2003, and some copies of that edition came with edible gummy worms in the jewel case. Rumors that they were hallucinogenic circulated; all parties denied it, according to Wikipedia. The 2024 anniversary edition reused the worm idea in its artwork.

years.h: First collaboration: Black: Implication Flooding with Keiji Haino
years.p: Boris teams up with the Japanese experimental musician Keiji Haino, the first of many collaborations.

years.h: Flood: 70 minutes in four movements
years.p: Recorded in September at Bazooka Studio, one title track that drifts from mechanical to ambient.
years.xp: It won little attention at first but became a cult record. In 2013 the band played the whole thing every night of a US residency tour, per Wikipedia.

years.h: Akuma no Uta: recorded to tape in one take
years.p: Cut January to March 2003 on analog tape. Pitchfork later put it at 198 on its 2000s albums list.
years.xp: The 2005 US release on Southern Lord ran 39 minutes against the Japanese 32, the length of Nick Drake's Bryter Layter, and its cover paid homage to Drake. The limited picture-disc tribute went to Venom instead.

years.h: Feedbacker is one 43-minute piece in five movements
years.p: Released on Diwphalanx in 2003. Boris later played it whole at All Tomorrow's Parties in 2009 and 2010.

eras.title: Pink and the Western breakthrough
eras.text: A hot-pink record with a fuzz-pop heart and a Sunn O))) collaboration bring Boris to Western ears. Southern Lord is the US home for the run.

years.h: Pink comes out in Japan, then blows up abroad
years.p: Released November 18, 2005 by Diwphalanx, reissued in 2006 by Southern Lord with new artwork and running order.
years.xp: Pitchfork gave it 8.7 and Spin an A; Blender and Spin named it among the best albums of 2006, per Wikipedia. The Nashville Scene called it the album that made metal hip. Its song "Farewell" appeared in Jim Jarmusch's The Limits of Control.

years.cap: Taken at the Biltmore nightclub in Vancouver in October 2011 · Wikimedia
years.h: Altar: Boris and Sunn O))) make one record
years.p: Southern Lord released it on Halloween 2006, recorded by Randall Dunn, with guests including Kim Thayil, Joe Preston and Jesse Sykes.
years.xp: The nine-track album stretches to a 28-minute finale, "Her Lips Were Wet With Venom." Pitchfork gave it 6.6 and PopMatters 8/10. Invisible Oranges credits it as pivotal for the band's US profile.

years.h: Blender, Spin and Pitchfork all list Pink
years.p: It placed in Pitchfork's Top 50 Records of 2006 and topped Exclaim!'s metal readers' poll, according to Wikipedia.

years.h: Smile: the band calls it the sell-out album
years.p: Michio Kurihara and Stephen O'Malley guest. Boris told Terrorizer it was uncool and their sell-out record.
years.xp: Diwphalanx released it in Japan and Southern Lord in the US with different art and tracklist. It reached number 20 on Billboard's Heatseekers chart, per Wikipedia.

years.h: Boris opens for Nine Inch Nails on the Lights in the Sky tour
years.p: Per Wikipedia, the trio supports [[Nine Inch Nails|b7ffd2af-418f-4be2-bdd1-22f8b48613da]] in North American arenas that year.

eras.title: Stretching out
eras.text: Boris plays whole albums live, scores a Jarmusch film and jumps between labels. Michio Kurihara, ex-Ghost, joins as a second guitarist. The band keeps releasing collaborations with Merzbow and Ian Astbury.

years.h: Boris performs Feedbacker whole at All Tomorrow's Parties
years.p: The Flaming Lips curated the 2009 ATP; Boris played the full 43-minute piece there and again at Pavement's 2010 edition.

years.h: Boris is on the soundtrack of Jim Jarmusch's The Limits of Control
years.p: "Farewell" from Pink appears in the film. Jarmusch likened their live shows to jazz musicians' improvising.

years.h: New Album leans into J-pop, on Sargent House
years.p: Its US release begins a run on Sargent House that lasts through Noise (2014) and Dear (2017).

years.h: Boris plays Flood in full every night of a US residency
years.p: The four-movement 2000 album becomes the centerpiece of the tour, per Wikipedia.

years.h: Noise: the band's most all-encompassing record
years.p: Released June 17 internationally on Sargent House, with a North American tour after. Pitchfork gave it 7.8.

eras.title: Thirty years and still heavy
eras.text: Boris marks 25 years with an album meant as a farewell, changes its mind, and makes NOW-era records in the pandemic. Heavy Rocks returns as a title for the third time.

q: We wanted to create music that we could leave behind.
years.h: Dear, made as a possible last album
years.p: For the 25th anniversary Boris made Dear on Sargent House, thinking it might be the last.
years.xp: Takeshi told Bandcamp Daily the group had made it because 25 years in a band can bring problems at home. The sessions went so well that the band kept going, and unused material was saved for later releases.

years.h: Pandemic project NOW: rock album NO, ambient album W
years.p: NO comes out in 2020, self-released, and W follows in 2021.

years.h: Heavy Rocks is a title for the third time
years.p: Relapse released the 30th anniversary album, after earlier records of the same name in 2002 and 2011.
years.xp: Ten tracks in 41 minutes, with singles "She Is Burning," "Question 1" and "My Name Is Blank." AllMusic's Thom Jurek called them feral and in a class of their own.

years.h: Fade, a drone metal record, arrives with no warning
years.p: Boris released it the same year as Heavy Rocks, per Wikipedia.

eras.title: Back to the roots
eras.text: The band keeps going and revisits its earliest records.

years.h: Amplifier Worship gets a 25th anniversary edition
years.p: The reissue's new art is based on the gummy worms that came with the 2003 Southern Lord CD.

sources.title: Invisible Oranges: So Grim So True So Real: Boris
